[3] (ran3_tdoc_chunks R3-214797, sim=0.6629)
The list of problems to be addressed in this work was initially agreed at RAN3 #112 meeting: an indicator of CHO, signalling for the early data forwarding to the target SN, enhancements to avoid over-booking of resources at the SN. Since that meeting nothing has changed. Also, in their most recent LS, RAN2 does not indicate any change in the scope of the problem. Therefore, it may be assumed the conclusions of the discussion in RAN3 are still relevant. Proposal 2-1: RAN3 shall confirm the scope of the solution as agreed at RAN3 #112 (i.e. an indicator of CHO, signalling for the early data forwarding to the target SN, enhancements to avoid over-booking of resources at the SN).

[5] (ran3_tdoc_chunks R3-190808, sim=0.6552)
At RAN3 #101bis, it was observed that Tracking Areas should be fixed with respect to the ground [1]. This seems to maintain current working practices in the Core Network, ensuring that e.g. paging may continue to work as closely as possible to legacy terrestrial networks. However, in [2] there is at least one instance where TAs are assumed to be moving with respect to the ground. We believe RAN3 should clarify once and for all whether TAs are stationary or not, and we propose some observations on potential trade-offs between the two cases.

The list of problems to be addressed in this work was initially agreed at RAN3 #112 meeting: an indicator of CHO, signalling for the early data forwarding to the target SN, enhancements to avoid over-booking of resources at the SN. Since that meeting nothing has changed. Also, in their most recent LS, RAN2 does not indicate any change in the scope of the problem. Therefore, it may be assumed the conclusions of the discussion in RAN3 are still relevant. Proposal 2-1: RAN3 shall confirm the scope of the solution as agreed at RAN3 #112 (i.e. an indicator of CHO, signalling for the early data forwarding to the target SN, enhancements to avoid over-booking of resources at the SN).
